initialFailure.response:
Nothing was installed or run on a Mac. The procedure below comes from `README.md` and the skill's install reference; I couldn't test the commands here because this session is on Linux.

**One catch:** the README's step 1 (fetch the skill from GitHub) currently gives you an incomplete skill. The public `main` branch has only `SKILL.md` and `references/editorial-checks.md`, and `references/installation.md` returns 404. The copy next to this README at `.claude/skills/screenrec/` is complete, so use that instead. The sparse-checkout route is also out on a new Mac, since it needs Git and the README says not to install Xcode or Command Line Tools just for that.

I've assumed your agent is Claude Code; the README doesn't cover installing the agent itself.

## 0. Preflight (on the Mac)

```sh
uname -m                  # must print arm64
sw_vers -productVersion   # must be 26.0 or newer
```

## 1. Install the screenrec skill

Copy the whole `.claude/skills/screenrec/` folder from this workspace (`SKILL.md` plus all four files in `references/`) to the Mac at:

```
~/.claude/skills/screenrec/
```

- **Codex CLI instead:** use `~/.agents/skills/screenrec/` and invoke with `$screenrec`.
- **Existing folder:** don't overwrite a `screenrec` skill that's already there; review it first.
- **Confirm:** start a new agent session and check that `screenrec` appears in the skill list (`/screenrec` in Claude Code).

## 2. Download and verify the latest stable release

The latest stable release is currently `v0.1.1`, and it has the three assets the README names.

```sh
(
  set -eu
  screenrec_download=$(mktemp -d)
  cd "$screenrec_download"
  curl -fL https://api.github.com/repos/dzhng/screen-recorder/releases/latest -o latest.json
  screenrec_tag=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract tag_name raw -o - latest.json)
  screenrec_release="https://github.com/dzhng/screen-recorder/releases/download/$screenrec_tag"
  curl -fL "$screenrec_release/ScreenRecorder-$screenrec_tag-macos-arm64.zip" -o "ScreenRecorder-$screenrec_tag-macos-arm64.zip"
  curl -fL "$screenrec_release/release.json" -o release.json
  curl -fL "$screenrec_release/SHA256SUMS" -o SHA256SUMS
  shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
  cat release.json
  ditto -x -k "ScreenRecorder-$screenrec_tag-macos-arm64.zip" unpacked
  printf 'Verified release extracted at: %s\n' "$screenrec_download/unpacked"
)
```

- **Checksum:** stop if `shasum` reports a failure.
- **Receipt:** check that `release.json` names the tag, `arm64` and a compatible minimum macOS. Today it shows `v0.1.1`, `arm64`, `minimumMacOS: 26.0`, `signature: ad-hoc`, `notarized: false`.
- **Keep the files:** hold on to the ZIP and receipt until the install is verified.

## 3. Install the app and launcher

Replace the placeholder with the path printed at the end of step 2.

```sh
(
  set -eu
  screenrec_unpacked="/absolute/path/printed/above/unpacked"
  screenrec_app="$HOME/Applications/Screen Recorder.app"
  screenrec_launcher="$HOME/.local/bin/screenrec"
  test ! -e "$screenrec_app"
  test ! -L "$screenrec_app"
  test ! -e "$screenrec_launcher"
  test ! -L "$screenrec_launcher"
  mkdir -p "$HOME/Applications" "$HOME/.local/bin"
  ditto "$screenrec_unpacked/Screen Recorder.app" "$screenrec_app"
  cp "$screenrec_unpacked/screenrec" "$screenrec_launcher"
  chmod +x "$screenrec_launcher"
)
```

Then put the launcher on PATH for this session and future ones:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

The docs only say to use your shell configuration or the agent's launch environment; `~/.zshrc` is my choice for the default macOS shell. Node is bundled, so you don't need Node, Bun, Swift, Git or a source build.

## 4. Verify before operating

```sh
command -v screenrec
screenrec capture.status --help   # returns a JSON schema; does not launch the app
screenrec service.health          # may launch the app's local service; never starts recording
```

- **Reading the result:** parse the JSON from `service.health` and check `ok` and the service status. Help succeeding on its own does not prove the service is ready.
- **If macOS blocks the launch:** open the installed app once, then approve System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Open Anyway**. This is expected because the build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. Don't strip quarantine attributes or disable Gatekeeper, and note that a managed Mac may forbid the override.
- **Not covered by install:** screen, microphone and camera permissions are separate approvals you grant later, and speech models are not downloaded.

Once step 1 is done, you can have the agent do steps 2–4 by asking it: "Use the screenrec skill to install the app and verify the CLI."
